cues.en: Anyway, I believe I've killed enough time. So ladies and gentlemen, a person who in this crowd needs absolutely no introduction, Cory Doctorow. So when I speak in places where the first language of the nation is not English, there is a disclaimer and an apology because I am one of nature's fast talkers.
cues.zh: 总之，我想我磨蹭的时间也够久了。那么女士们先生们，有请一位在座各位都无人不晓的人物，Cory Doctorow。每次在母语非英语的地方演讲，我都要先声明并致歉，因为我天生语速就极快。

cues.en: When I was at the United Nations at the World Intellectual Property Organization, I was known as the scourge of the simultaneous translation corps. I would stand up and speak and turn around and there would be window after window of translator and every one of them would be doing this. So in advance, I give you permission when I start talking quickly to do this and I will slow down. So tonight's talk...
cues.zh: 当年我在联合国的世界知识产权组织时，是出了名的“同传杀手”。每次我起身发言，回头一看，一排排翻译间里的译员全都在冲我摆手比划。所以先说好，要是我语速飙起来了，允许你们冲我比这个手势，我会慢下来的。那么，今晚的演讲……

cues.en: tonight's talk is not a copyright talk I do copyright talks all the time questions about culture and creativity are interesting enough but to be honest I'm quite sick of them if you want to hear freelance writers like me bang on about what's happening to the way that we earn our living by all means go and find one of the many talks I've done on this subject on YouTube but tonight I want to talk about something more important
cues.zh: 今晚的演讲不是关于版权的。我成天讲版权，文化和创意方面的问题固然很有趣，但说实话，我都快讲吐了。如果你想听像我这样的自由撰稿人唠叨我们的生计受到了什么冲击，大可以在 YouTube 上搜到很多我关于这个话题的演讲，但今晚我想聊些更重要的事情。

cues.en: I want to talk about general purpose computers. Because general purpose computers are in fact astounding. So astounding that our society is still struggling to come to grips with them, to figure out what they're for, to figure out how to accommodate them and how to cope with them. Which, unfortunately, brings me back to copyright. Because the general shape of the copyright wars and the lessons they can teach us
cues.zh: 我想聊聊通用计算机。因为通用计算机实在是太惊人了。惊人到我们的社会至今仍在艰难地理解它、弄清它的用途、想办法去适应它并应对它。遗憾的是，这又让我绕回了版权问题。因为版权大战的大致格局，以及它能带给我们的启示，

cues.en: about the upcoming fights over the destiny of the general purpose computer are important. In the beginning, we had packaged software and the attendant industry, and we had sneaker net. So we had floppy disks in Ziploc bags or in cardboard boxes, hung on pegs in shops, and sold like candy bars and magazines. And they were eminently susceptible to duplication, and so...
cues.zh: 对于即将到来的关乎通用计算机命运的抗争至关重要。最初，我们有了盒装软件和随之而来的产业，当时靠的是“跑腿网络”（sneaker net）。软盘装在自封袋或纸盒里，挂在店里的挂钩上，像糖果和杂志一样售卖。它们极易被复制，所以……

cues.en: They were duplicated quickly and widely, and this was to the great chagrin of people who made and sold software. Enter DRM 0.96. They started to introduce physical defects to the disks, or started to insist on other physical indicia, which the software could check for, dongles, hidden sectors, challenge response protocols that required that you had physical possession of large, unwieldy manuals that were difficult to copy.
cues.zh: 它们被迅速且广泛地复制，这让开发和销售软件的人大为头疼。于是 DRM 0.96 登场了。他们开始在磁盘上制造物理坏道，或者非要加入其他物理特征让软件来检测，比如加密狗、隐藏扇区，或是挑战-应答协议，要求你手头必须有一本极难复印的厚重手册。

cues.en: And of course, these failed for two reasons. First, they were commercially unpopular, of course, because they reduced the usefulness of the software to the legitimate purchasers while leaving the people who took the software without paying for it untouched. The legitimate purchasers resented the non-functionality of their backups. They hated the loss of scarce ports to the authentication dongles, and they resented the inconvenience of having to transport large manuals when they wanted to run their software.
cues.zh: 当然，这些尝试由于两个原因失败了。首先在商业上很不受欢迎，因为它们降低了软件对正版买家的实用性，却完全奈何不了白嫖软件的人。正版买家反感备份盘无法使用，讨厌宝贵的接口被认证加密狗占用，更受不了每次想运行软件还得随身带本大厚书。

cues.en: And second, these didn't stop pirates who found it trivial to patch the software and bypass authentication. Typically, the way that happened is some expert who had possession of technology and expertise of equivalent sophistication to the software vendor itself would reverse engineer the software and release cracked versions that quickly became widely circulated. While this kind of expertise and technology sounded highly specialized, it really wasn't.
cues.zh: 其次，这些并没有阻止盗版者，他们发现给软件打补丁、绕过认证轻而易举。通常发生的方式是，某个掌握与软件厂商同等复杂技术和专业知识的专家会逆向工程软件，发布破解版，很快便广泛流传。虽然这种专业技能听起来高度专门化，其实并不是。

cues.en: Figuring out what recalcitrant programs were doing and routing around the defects in shitty floppy disk media were both core skills for computer programmers and were even more so in the era of fragile floppy disks and the rough and ready early days of software development. Anti-copying strategies only became more fraught as networks spread.
cues.zh: 弄懂顽固程序在干什么，以及绕过劣质软盘介质中的缺陷，都是计算机程序员的核心技能；在脆弱软盘和软件开发粗放早期，更是如此。随着网络扩散，反拷贝策略只会变得更加棘手。

cues.en: Once we had BBSs, online services, Usenet news groups and mailing lists, the expertise of people who figured out how to defeat these authentication systems could be packaged up in software and passed around as little crack files, or as the network capacity increased, the crack disk images or executables themselves could be spread on their own, which gave us DRM 1.0.
cues.zh: 有了 BBS、在线服务、Usenet 新闻组和邮件列表之后，那些弄明白如何攻破这些认证系统的人，其专业知识可以被封装进软件，作为小小的破解文件传播；或者随着网络容量提升，破解磁盘镜像或可执行文件本身就能独立传播，这便带来了 DRM 1.0。

cues.en: By 1996, it became clear to everyone in the halls of power that there was something important about to happen. We were about to have an information economy, whatever the hell that was. They assumed it meant an economy where we bought and sold information. Now, information technology makes things efficient, so imagine the markets.
cues.zh: 到1996年，权力机构里的所有人都清楚，有件重要的事即将发生。我们即将进入信息经济——不管那到底是什么鬼。他们以为这意味着一个买卖信息的经济。现在，信息技术让一切变得高效，所以想象一下那些市场吧。

cues.en: that an information economy would have. You could buy a book for a day. You could sell the right to watch the movie for one euro. And then you could rent out the pause button at one penny per second. You could sell movies for one price in one country and another price in another.
cues.zh: 一个信息经济将会拥有的市场。你可以按天买一本书。你可以用一欧元出售电影观看权。然后还能以每秒一便士出租暂停键。你可以在一个国家一个价、另一个国家另一个价卖电影。

cues.en: And so on and so on, the fantasies of those days were a little like a boring science fiction adaptation of the Old Testament book of numbers. A kind of tedious enumeration of every permutation of things people do with information and the ways we could charge them for it. But none of this would be possible unless we could control how people use their computers.
cues.zh: 如此等等。那些日子的幻想，有点像把旧约《民数记》改编成无聊科幻片。无非是乏味地罗列人们用信息所做之事的每一种排列组合，以及我们能如何收费。但除非我们能控制人们如何使用电脑，这一切都不可能实现。

cues.en: and the files that we transferred to them. After all, it was well and good to talk about selling someone the 24-hour write to a video, or the right to move music onto an iPod, but not the right to move music from the iPod onto another device. But how the hell could you do that once you'd given them the file? In order to make this work, you needed to figure out how to stop computers from running certain programs and inspecting certain files and processes. For example,
cues.zh: 以及我们传送给他们的文件。毕竟，说要把视频的24小时使用权卖给别人，或者把音乐移入 iPod 的权利卖给别人，但不给从 iPod 移到另一台设备的权利，这当然好听。可一旦把文件给了他们，你到底怎么可能做到？为了让这套东西成立，你得想办法阻止电脑运行某些程序、检查某些文件和进程。例如，

cues.en: you could encrypt the file and then require the user to run a program that only unlocked the file under certain circumstances. But as they say on the internet, now you have two problems. You also now have to stop the user from saving the file while it's in the clear, and you have to stop the user from figuring out where the unlocking program stores its keys, because if the user finds the keys, she'll just decrypt the file and throw away that stupid player app. And now you have three problems, because now...
cues.zh: 你可以加密文件，然后要求用户运行一个只在特定情况下解锁文件的程序。但正如网上所说，现在你有两个问题了。你现在还得阻止用户在文件处于明文时保存它，并且得阻止用户弄清解锁程序把密钥存在哪里；因为一旦用户找到密钥，她就会直接解密文件，扔掉那个破播放器应用。现在你有三个问题了，因为现在……

cues.en: You have to stop the users who figure out how to render the file on the clear from sharing it with other users. And now you've got four problems, because now you have to stop the users who figure out how to extract secrets from unlocking programs from telling other users how to do it too. And now you've got five problems, because now you have to stop users who figure out how to extract secrets from unlocking programs from telling other users what the secrets were. That's a lot of problems.
cues.zh: 你得阻止那些搞懂怎么把文件解密渲染出来的用户，不让他们分享给别人。现在你有了四个难题，因为你还得阻止那些搞懂怎么从解锁程序中提取密钥的用户，不让他们教别人怎么做。接着你又有了五个难题，因为你还得阻止那些搞懂怎么从解锁程序中提取密钥的用户，不让他们告诉别人密钥到底是什么。这下问题可真够多的。

cues.en: But by 1996, we had a solution. We had the WIPO copyright treaty passed by the United Nations World Intellectual Property Organization, which created laws that made it illegal to extract secrets from unlocking programs. And it created laws that made it illegal to extract media clear texts from the unlocking programs while they were running. And it created laws that made it illegal to tell people how to extract secrets from unlocking programs. And it created laws that made it illegal to host copyrighted works and secrets.
cues.zh: 但到了 1996 年，我们有了解决方案。联合国世界知识产权组织通过了 WIPO 版权条约，它确立了相关法律，规定从解锁程序中提取密钥是违法的。它还确立了法律，规定在解锁程序运行时从中提取媒体明文是违法的。它还确立了法律，规定教别人如何从解锁程序中提取密钥也是违法的。它甚至确立了法律，规定托管受版权保护的作品和密钥统统违法。

cues.en: and all with a handy, streamlined process that lets you remove stuff from the internet without having to screw around with lawyers and judges and all that crap. And with that, illegal copying ended forever. The information economy blossomed into a beautiful flower that brought prosperity to the whole wide world, as they say on the aircraft carriers, mission accomplished. Well, of course, that's not how the story ends because...
cues.zh: 而且这一切都配有一套简便、高效的流程，让你不必跟律师、法官这类破事纠缠，就能直接把网上的内容撤下来。就这样，非法复制被彻底终结了。信息经济开出了一朵绚丽的花朵，给全世界带来了繁荣，正如航空母舰上那句名言所说：“任务完成”。好吧，故事当然不可能就这么结束，因为……

cues.en: pretty much anyone who understood computers and networks understood that while these laws would create more problems than they could possibly solve. After all, these were laws that made it illegal to look inside your computer when it was running certain programs. They made it illegal to tell people what you found when you looked inside your computer. They made it easy to censor material on the internet without having to prove that anything wrong had happened. In short, they made unrealistic demands on reality, and reality did not oblige them. After all,
cues.zh: 几乎每个懂计算机和网络的人都明白，这些法律制造的问题远比它们能解决的多得多。毕竟，这些法律竟然规定，在计算机运行某些程序时查看其内部运作是违法的。它们规定，把你检查计算机时发现的东西告诉别人是违法的。它们让审查互联网内容变得轻而易举，甚至无需证明确实存在侵权行为。简而言之，它们对现实提出了不切实际的要求，而现实根本不买账。毕竟，

cues.en: copying only got easier following the passage of these laws copying will only ever get easier here 2011 this is as hard as copying will get your grandchildren will turn to you around the Christmas table and say tell me again grandpa tell me again grandma about when it was hard to copy things in 2011 when you couldn't get a drive the size of your fingernail that could hold every song ever recorded every movie ever made every word ever spoken every picture ever taken everything and transferred in such a short period of time you didn't even know
cues.zh: 在这些法律通过之后，复制只会变得越来越容易；复制永远只可能越来越容易；现在是 2011 年，眼下已经是复制门槛最高的时候了；你的孙子孙女会在圣诞餐桌旁围着你问：“爷爷/奶奶，再给我们讲讲 2011 年复制东西有多难吧，那时候你还没法搞到一个指甲盖大小的硬盘，装下有史以来的每首歌、每部电影、每句说过的话、每张拍过的照片，装下所有东西，而且传输速度快到你都感觉不到

cues.en: it was doing it, tell us again when it was so stupidly hard to copy things back in 2011. And so reality asserted itself and everyone had a good laugh over how funny our misconceptions were when we entered the 21st century and then a lasting peace was reached with freedom and prosperity for all. Well, not really. Because like the nursery rhyme lady who swallows a spider to catch a fly and then has to swallow a bird to catch the spider and a cat to catch the bird and so on,
cues.zh: 它在传输，再给我们讲讲 2011 年复制东西怎么会那么费劲吧。”于是现实给出了答案，每个人都对我们迈入 21 世纪时有多么愚蠢的误解付之一笑，随后迎来了持久的和平，人人享有自由与繁荣。好吧，其实并没有。因为就像童谣里那位为了吞苍蝇而吞下蜘蛛，又为了吞蜘蛛而不得不吞下鸟儿，再为了吞鸟儿而吞下猫咪的老太太一样，

cues.en: So must a regulation that has broad general appeal but is disastrous in its implementation, but get a new regulation aimed at shoring up the failure of the old one. Now it's tempting to stop the story here and conclude that the problem is that lawmakers are either clueless or evil or possibly evilly clueless and just leave it there, which is not a very satisfying place to go because it's fundamentally a council of despair.
cues.zh: 一项表面上广受欢迎、但在执行上堪称灾难的监管法规，必然会衍生出一项旨在弥补旧法规失败的新法规。现在我们很想把故事停在这里，并得出结论：问题在于立法者要么一无所知，要么心怀叵测，或者干脆是恶毒的蠢货，然后就此作罢，但这并不是个让人满意的结论，因为这从根本上说只是一种绝望的妥协。

cues.en: It suggests that our problems cannot be solved for so long as stupidity and evilness are present in the halls of power, which is to say they will never be solved. But I have another theory about what's happened. It's not that regulators don't understand information technology, because it should be possible to be a non-expert and still make a good law. MPs and congressmen and so on are elected to represent districts and people, not disciplines and issues.
cues.zh: 这暗示只要权力殿堂里还有愚蠢和邪恶，我们的问题就无解，也就是说永远解决不了。但对于发生了什么，我有另一种理论。并不是监管者不懂信息技术，因为不是专家也应当能制定出好法律。议员和国会议员等是代表选区和人民选出的，不是代表学科和议题。

cues.en: We don't have a member of parliament for biochemistry and we don't have a senator from the great state of urban planning and we don't have an MEP from child welfare. But perhaps we should. And yet those people who are experts in policy and politics and not technical disciplines nevertheless often do manage to pass good rules that make sense. And that's because government relies on heuristics, rules of thumb about how to balance out expert input from different sides of an issue.
cues.zh: 我们没有生物化学选区的议员，没有来自“城市规划伟大州”的参议员，也没有代表儿童福利的欧洲议会议员。但也许我们应该有。然而，那些精通政策和政治、而非技术学科的人，却常常能通过合理的好规则。这是因为政府依赖启发式方法，也就是关于如何权衡问题各方专家意见的经验法则。

cues.en: But information technology confounds these heuristics. It kicks the crap out of them in one important way. And this is it. One important test of whether or not a regulation is fit for purpose is first whether, of course, it will work. But second of all, whether or not in the course of doing its work, it will have lots of effects on everything else. If I wanted Congress or Parliament or the EU to regulate a wheel, it's unlikely I'd succeed.
cues.zh: 但信息技术让这些启发式方法失灵。它在一个重要方面把它们打得落花流水。就是这个。检验一项监管是否适用，一个重要标准首先是它当然得管用。其次是在履行其职责的过程中，它是否会对其他一切产生大量影响。如果我想让国会、议会或欧盟去监管轮子，我不太可能成功。

cues.en: If I turned up and said, well, everyone knows wheels are good and right, but have you noticed that every single bank robber has four wheels on his car when he drives away from the bank robbery? Can't we do something about this? The answer would, of course, be no. Because we don't know how to make a wheel that is still generally useful for legitimate wheel applications, but useless to bad guys.
cues.zh: 如果我跑去说，大家都知道轮子是好的、对的，但你们注意到没有，每个银行劫匪开车逃离银行时，车上都有四个轮子？我们就不能想想办法吗？答案当然是不行。因为我们不知道怎么造出一种轮子，既对合法的轮子用途普遍有用，又对坏人没用。

cues.en: And we can all see that the general benefits of wheels are so profound that we'd be foolish to risk them in a foolish errand to stop bank robberies by changing wheels. Even if there were an epidemic of bank robberies, even if society were on the verge of collapse thanks to bank robberies, no one would think that wheels were the right place to start solving our problems. But if I were to show up in that same body to say that I had absolute proof that hands-free phones...
cues.zh: 我们都能看到，轮子的普遍益处如此巨大，以至于为了阻止银行抢劫去改轮子，拿这些益处冒险，那就太愚蠢了。即使银行抢劫成灾，即使社会因银行抢劫濒临崩溃，也没人会认为轮子是解决问题的正确起点。但如果我出现在同一个机构，说我有绝对证据证明免提手机……

cues.en: were making cars dangerous. And I said, I would like you to pass a law that says it's illegal to put a hands-free phone in a car. The regulator might say, yeah, I take your point. We'll do that. And we might disagree about whether or not this is a good idea, whether or not my evidence made sense. But very few of us would say, well, once you take the hands-free phones out of the car, they stop being cars.
cues.zh: 正在让汽车变得危险。我会说，我希望你们通过一项法律，规定在车里装免提手机是非法的。监管者可能会说，好，我明白你的意思。我们会照做。我们可能对这是不是个好主意、我的证据是否站得住脚有分歧。但很少有人会说，好吧，一旦把免提手机从车里拿走，它们就不再是汽车了。

cues.en: We understand that we can keep cars' cars even if we remove features from them. Cars are special purpose, at least in comparison to wheels. And all that the addition of a hands-free phone does is add one more feature to an already specialized technology. In fact, there's the heuristic that we can apply here. Special purpose technologies are complex. And you can remove features from them without doing fundamental disfiguring violence to their underlying utility.
cues.zh: 我们明白，就算去掉某些功能，汽车也依然是汽车。至少跟轮子比起来，汽车属于专用技术。给车加装免提电话，不过是在原本就高度专用的技术上多添了一项功能而已。事实上，我们这里可以套用一条经验法则：专用技术本身很复杂，你可以从中剥离掉某些功能，却不会对它的核心功用造成根本性的破坏。

cues.en: This rule of thumb serves regulators well by and large, but it is rendered null and void by the general purpose computer and the general purpose network, the PC and the internet. Because if you think of computer software as a feature, that is, a computer with spreadsheets running on it has a spreadsheet feature and one that's running World of Warcraft has an MMORPG feature.
cues.zh: 监管者通常很受用这条经验法则，但遇到通用计算机和通用网络——也就是 PC 和互联网时，它就彻底失效了。因为如果你把计算机软件看作一种功能，比如电脑运行电子表格就是拥有表格功能，运行《魔兽世界》就是拥有大型多人在线角色扮演功能，

cues.en: then this heuristic leads you to think that you could reasonably say, make me a computer that doesn't run spreadsheets, and that it would be no more an attack on computing than make me a car without a hands-free phone is an attack on cars. And if you think of protocols and sites as features of the network, then saying, fix the internet so that it doesn't run BitTorrent, or fix the internet so that the piratebay.org no longer resolves, it sounds a lot like
cues.zh: 那么这种直觉就会让你以为，提一句“给我造一台不能运行电子表格的电脑”是完全合情合理的，这就好比要求“造一辆没有免提电话的车”，根本算不上是对汽车本身的攻击。同理，如果你把协议和网站当成网络的功能，那么说“整改一下互联网，让它跑不了 BitTorrent”，或者“整顿一下网络，让 piratebay.org 无法解析”，听起来就很像是

cues.en: Change the sound of busy signals or take that pizzeria on the corner off the phone network and not like an attack on the fundamental principles of internet working Not realizing that the thumb that this rule of thumb that works for cars and houses and every other substantial area of technological Regulation fails for the internet does not make you evil and it does not make you an ignoramus It just makes you part of that vast majority of the world for whom ideas like touring complete and end-to-end are meaningless
cues.zh: “改一下电话忙音的提示声”，或者“把街角那家披萨店从电话网里除名”，完全不觉得这是在撼动网络互联的根本原则。没有意识到这套适用于汽车、房屋以及几乎所有实体技术监管领域的经验法则在互联网上会失灵，并不意味着你居心叵测，也不意味着你愚昧无知，这只说明你和世上绝大多数人一样，对“图灵完备”和“端到端”这类概念完全不解其意。

cues.en: So our regulators go off and they blithely pass these laws and they become part of the reality of our technological world. There are suddenly numbers that we aren't allowed to write down on the internet, programs we're not allowed to publish, and all it takes to make legitimate material disappear from the internet is to say that that infringes copyright.
cues.zh: 于是我们的监管者们行事了，他们轻松愉快地通过了这些法案，让它们变成了我们技术世界的现实。突然之间，互联网上有了我们不能写下来的数字、不能发布的程序；而且只要宣称某样东西侵犯了版权，就能让合法的内容从网上凭空消失。

cues.en: It fails to attain the actual goal of the regulation. It doesn't stop people from violating copyright. But it bears a kind of superficial resemblance to copyright enforcement. It satisfies the security syllogism. Something must be done. I am doing something. Something has been done. And thus, any failures that arise can be blamed on the idea that the regulation doesn't go far enough, rather than the idea that it was flawed from the outset.
cues.zh: 这种做法根本达不到监管的真正目的，它并不能阻止人们侵犯版权。但它表面上看着很像是在执行版权保护，恰好迎合了那种安全逻辑的三段论：“必须得做点什么；我正在做点什么；事情已经解决了。”如此一来，后续出现的任何失败，都可以归咎于监管力度还不够大，而不是去承认它从一开始就存在根本缺陷。

cues.en: This kind of superficial resemblance and underlying divergence happens in other engineering contexts. I have a friend who was once a senior executive at a big consumer packaged goods company who told me about what happened when the marketing department told the engineers that they thought up a great idea for detergent. From now on, they were going to make detergent that made your clothes newer every time you wash them. Well, after the engineers had tried unsuccessfully to convey the concept of entropy to the marketing department, they arrived at another solution.
cues.zh: 这种表面相似、本质背离的情况也出现在其他工程领域。我有个朋友曾在一家大型快消品公司做高管，他跟我讲过营销部门告诉工程师他们想出了一个洗涤剂的好点子之后发生的事。从今往后，他们要做一种洗涤剂，让你每次洗衣服衣服都变得更“新”。工程师们没能成功向营销部门解释熵的概念，于是他们想出了另一个解决方案。

cues.en: solution. They developed a detergent that used enzymes that attacked loose fiber ends, which were the kind that you get with broken fibers that made your clothes look old. So every time you washed your clothes in the detergent, they would look newer. That was because the detergent was literally digesting your clothes. Using it would cause your clothes to literally dissolve in the washing machine.
cues.zh: 解决方案。他们开发了一种洗涤剂，用酶去攻击松散纤维末端，也就是纤维断裂后产生、让你衣服显旧的那种末端。于是每次用这种洗涤剂洗衣服，衣服看起来都会更新。那是因为这种洗涤剂真的在消化你的衣服。使用它会让你的衣服在洗衣机里真的溶解掉。

cues.en: This was the opposite of making clothes newer. Instead, you are artificially aging your clothes every time you wash them. And as a user, the more you deployed the solution, the more drastic your measures had to be to keep your clothes up to date. You actually had to go buy new clothes because the old ones fell apart. So today we have marketing departments who say things like, we don't need computers, we need...
cues.zh: 这与让衣服变新恰恰相反。相反，你每次洗衣服都在人为加速衣服老化。而且作为用户，你越是用这个方案，就越得采取更极端的手段让衣服保持“时新”。你实际上得去买新衣服，因为旧衣服已经散架了。所以今天我们有营销部门会说，我们不需要计算机，我们需要……

cues.en: appliances. Make me a computer that doesn't run every program, just a program that does this specialized task like streaming audio or routing packets or playing Xbox games and make sure it doesn't run programs that I haven't authorized that might undermine our profits. On the surface this seems like a reasonable idea.
cues.zh: 家电。给我造一台计算机，不要运行所有程序，只运行做这种专门任务的程序，比如流媒体音频、路由数据包或玩 Xbox 游戏，并确保它不运行我未授权、可能损害我们利润的程序。表面上看，这似乎是个合理的想法。

cues.en: Just a program that does one specialized task, like streaming, rather, after all, we can put an electric motor in a blender and we can install a motor in a dishwasher, and we don't worry about whether it's still possible to run a dishwashing program in a blender. But that's not what we do when we turn a computer into an appliance. We're not making a computer that only runs the appliance app.
cues.zh: 只是一个执行某项专门任务的程序，比如流媒体；毕竟，我们可以把电动机装进搅拌机，也可以把电动机装进洗碗机，而且我们不担心搅拌机里还能不能运行洗碗程序。但当我们把计算机变成家电时，我们并不是这么做的。我们不是在造一台只运行家电应用的计算机。

cues.en: We're making a computer that can run every program, but which uses some combination of rootkits, spyware, and code signing to prevent the user from knowing which processes are running, from installing her own software, and from terminating processes that she doesn't want. In other words, an appliance is not a stripped-down computer. It is a fully functional computer with spyware on it out of the box. Thanks.
cues.zh: 我们造的是一台能运行所有程序的计算机，但它会组合使用 rootkit、间谍软件和代码签名，让用户无法知道哪些进程在运行、无法安装自己的软件、也无法终止自己不想要的进程。换句话说，家电并不是精简版的计算机。它是一台开箱即带间谍软件、功能完整的计算机。谢谢。

cues.en: Because we don't know how to build the general purpose computer that is capable of running every program we can compile except for some program that we don't like or that we prohibit by law or that loses us money. The closest approximation we have to this is a computer with spyware, a computer on which remote parties set policies without the computer user's knowledge over the objection of the computer's owner. And so it is that digital rights management always converges on malware.
cues.zh: 因为我们根本不知道该怎么造出一台通用计算机，它既能运行我们编译出的所有程序，唯独不能运行那些我们不喜欢的、法律禁止的、或者让我们亏钱的程序。我们所能做出的最接近这种设想的，就是装了间谍软件的电脑，在这种电脑上，远程第三方可以在用户不知情且违背设备所有者意愿的情况下制定规则。正因如此，数字版权管理最终总是会演变成恶意软件。

cues.en: There was, of course, this famous incident, a kind of gift to people who have this hypothesis, in which Sony loaded covert rootkit installers on 6 million audio CDs, which secretly executed programs that watched for attempts to read the sound files on CDs and terminated them, and which also hid the rootkit's existence by causing the kernel to lie about which processes were running and which files were present on the drive. But it's not the only example. Just recently, Nintendo shipped the 3DS.
cues.zh: 当然，还有过这样一个著名的事件，对于持有这种假说的人来说简直是送上门的例证：Sony 曾在 600 万张音乐 CD 中植入了隐蔽的 Rootkit 安装程序，它会秘密运行并监控读取 CD 音频文件的企图然后将其终止，甚至还让内核在运行的进程和驱动器中的文件上说谎，以此掩盖这个 Rootkit 的存在。但这也绝非孤例。就在最近，Nintendo 推出了 3DS。

cues.en: which opportunistically updates its firmware and does an integrity check to make sure that you haven't altered the old firmware in any way, and if it detects signs of tampering, it bricks itself. Human rights activists have raised alarms over UFE, the new PC bootloader that restricts your computer, so it runs signed operating systems, noting that repressive governments will likely withhold signatures from OSs unless they have covert surveillance operations. And on the network side...
cues.zh: 它会伺机更新固件，并进行完整性检查以确保你没有以任何方式修改旧固件，一旦检测到篡改迹象，它就会直接变砖。人权活动人士也对 UFE 发出了警告，这种限制你电脑的新型 PC 引导加载程序只能运行带有签名的操作系统，他们指出，专制政府很可能会扣留操作系统的签名，除非系统内置了秘密监控功能。而在网络方面……

cues.en: attempts to make a network that can't be used for copyright infringement always converges with the surveillance and control measures that we know from repressive governments. So SOPA, the American U.S. Stop Online Piracy Act, bans tools like DNSSEC because they can be used to defeat DNS blocking measures. And it bans tools like Tor because they can be used to circumvent IP blocking measures. In fact...
cues.zh: 试图打造一个无法被用于侵犯版权的网络，其最终结果必然会走向我们在专制政府那里见过的监控与控制手段。所以 SOPA，也就是美国的《禁止网络盗版法案》，禁止了像 DNSSEC 这样的工具，因为它们可以用来破解 DNS 封锁手段。它还禁止了像 Tor 这样的工具，因为它们可以用来绕过 IP 封锁手段。事实上……

cues.en: The proponents of SOPA, the Motion Picture Association of America, circulated a memo citing research that SOPA would probably work because it uses the same measures as are used in Syria, China, and Uzbekistan, and they argue that these measures are effective in those countries, and so they would work in America too. Don't applaud me, applaud the MPAA.
cues.zh: SOPA 的支持者，也就是美国电影协会（MPAA），曾散发过一份备忘录，引用研究称 SOPA 很可能会起作用，因为它采用了与叙利亚、中国和乌兹别克斯坦相同的手段，他们辩称这些手段在那些国家很有效，所以在美洲也同样管用。别给我鼓掌，去给 MPAA 鼓掌吧。

cues.en: It may seem like SOPA is the endgame in a long fight over copyright and the internet, and it may seem like if we defeat SOPA, we'll be well on our way to securing the freedom of PCs and networks. But as I said at the beginning of this talk, this isn't about copyright, because the copyright wars are just the 0.9 beta version of the long-coming war on computation. The entertainment industry were just the first belligerents in this coming century-long conflict.
cues.zh: SOPA 看起来似乎是围绕版权与互联网长期争斗的终局之战，看起来只要我们打败了 SOPA，就能在确保 PC 和网络自由的道路上大步迈进。但正如我在演讲开始时所说的，这根本不是版权的问题，因为版权之战不过是这场旷日持久的计算控制权之战的 0.9 测试版。娱乐业仅仅是这场即将来临的百年冲突中的第一批交战方。

cues.en: We tend to think of them as particularly successful. After all, here is SOPA, trembling on the verge of passage and breaking the internet on this fundamental level in the name of preserving top 40 music, reality TV shows, and Ashton Kutcher movies. But the reality is that copyright legislation gets as far as it does precisely because it's not taken seriously.
cues.zh: 我们总觉得它们特别成功。毕竟，SOPA正颤巍巍地濒临通过，并以保护排行榜金曲、真人秀和Ashton Kutcher电影之名，在根本层面上搞垮互联网。但现实是，版权立法之所以能推进到这个地步，恰恰是因为没人把它当回事。

cues.en: which is why, on the one hand, Canada has had Parliament after Parliament introduce one stupid copyright law after another, but on the other hand, Parliament after Parliament has failed to actually vote on the bill. It's why we got SOPA, a bill composed of pure, stupid, pieced together, molecule by molecule, into a kind of stupidite 250 that is normally only found in the heart of a newborn star.
cues.zh: 所以一方面，加拿大一届又一届议会提出一个又一个愚蠢的版权法；另一方面，一届又一届议会却始终没真正对法案投票。这就是为什么会有SOPA——一项由纯粹的愚蠢逐分子拼凑而成的法案，堪称“蠢素-250”，通常只在新生恒星核心才找得到。

cues.en: And it's why this rush through SOPA hearings had to be adjourned midway through the Christmas break so that lawmakers could get into a real, vicious, nationally infamous debate over an important issue, unemployment insurance. It's why the World Intellectual Property Organization is gold time and again into enacting crazed pig ignorant copyright proposals.
cues.zh: 这也是为什么SOPA听证会赶得那么急，却不得不在圣诞假期中途休会，好让议员们就一个重要议题——失业保险——展开真正激烈、全国臭名昭著的辩论。这也是为什么WIPO被一再怂恿去通过疯狂又极其无知的版权提案。

cues.en: Because when the nations of the world send their UN missions to Geneva, they send water experts, not copyright experts. They send health experts, not copyright experts. They send agriculture experts, not copyright experts. Because copyright is just not important to pretty much everyone. Canada's Parliament didn't vote on its copyright bills because of all the things Canada needs to do.
cues.zh: 因为当世界各国向日内瓦派遣联合国代表团时，派的是水专家，不是版权专家；派的是卫生专家，不是版权专家；派的是农业专家，不是版权专家。因为对几乎所有人来说，版权根本不重要。加拿大议会没对版权法案投票，是因为加拿大有太多事要做。

cues.en: Fixing copyright ranks well below resolving health emergencies on First Nations reservations, exploiting the oil patch in Alberta, interceding in sectarian resentments among French and English speakers, solving resource crises in the nation's fisheries, and a thousand other issues. The triviality of copyright tells you that when other sectors of the economy start to avenge concerns about the internet and the PC, the copyright will be revealed for a minor skirmish and not a war.
cues.zh: 修复版权问题的优先级，远远低于解决原住民保留地的卫生紧急状况、开发阿尔伯塔油田、调停英法裔之间的群体积怨、解决全国渔业的资源危机，以及成千上万个其他问题。版权的琐碎性告诉你：当经济中其他行业开始就互联网和PC带来的担忧发难时，版权问题将暴露为一场小摩擦，而不是一场战争。

cues.en: Why would other sectors nurse grudges against computers well because the world we live in today is made of computers We don't have cars anymore. We have computers. We ride in we don't have airplanes anymore We have flying Solaris boxes with a big bucket full of SCADA controllers
cues.zh: 为什么其他行业会对计算机心怀怨恨？因为今天我们的世界是由计算机构成的。我们不再有汽车，我们有计算机；我们不再有飞机，我们有飞行的Solaris盒子，里面塞满一大桶SCADA控制器。

cues.en: A 3D printer is not a device. It's a peripheral and it only works connected to a computer. A radio is no longer a crystal. It's a general purpose computer with a fast ADC and a fast DAC and some software. The grievances that arose from unauthorized copying are trivial when compared to the calls for action that our new computer embroidered reality will create.
cues.zh: 3D打印机不是设备，而是外设，只有连上计算机才能工作。收音机不再是一块晶体，而是一台通用计算机，配有快速ADC、快速DAC和一些软件。与新的计算机编织现实将引发的行动呼吁相比，未经授权复制所引发的不满微不足道。

cues.en: Think of radio for a minute. The entire basis for radio regulation up until today was based on the idea that the properties of radio are fixed at the time of manufacture and can't be easily altered. You can't just flip a switch on your baby monitor and turn it into something that interferes with air traffic control signals. But powerful software-defined radios can change from baby monitor to emergency services dispatcher to air traffic controller just by loading and executing different software.
cues.zh: 不妨想想无线电。直到今天，整个无线电监管的基础都建立在一个假设上：无线电的特性在出厂时就已固定，无法轻易更改。你不可能随手拨一下婴儿监视器的开关，就把它变成能干扰空中交通管制信号的设备。但功能强大的软件定义无线电，只需加载并运行不同的软件，就能从婴儿监视器摇身变成应急调度台或空中管制的通信设备。

cues.en: Which is why the first time the American telecoms regulator, the FCC, considered what would happen when we put SDRs in the field, they asked for comment on whether it should mandate that all software-defined radios should be embedded in trusted computing machines. Ultimately, whether every PC should be locked so that the programs they run are strictly regulated by central authorities.
cues.zh: 正因如此，当美国电信监管机构 FCC 首次考虑广泛部署 SDR 会带来什么后果时，他们征求了公众意见，探讨是否应强制要求所有软件定义无线电都必须植入可信计算设备中。说到底，就是探讨是否该给每台 PC 都上一把锁，让它们运行的程序受到中央机构的严格监管。

cues.en: And even this is a shadow of what is to come. After all, this was the year in which we saw the debut of open-sourced shapefiles for converting AR-15s to full automatic. This was the year of crowdfunded open-sourced hardware for gene sequencing. And while 3D printing will give rise to plenty of trivial complaints, there will be judges in the American South and mullahs in Iran who will lose their minds over people in their jurisdiction printing out sex toys. The trajectory...
cues.zh: 而这还只是未来风暴的前兆。毕竟，正是在这一年，能将 AR-15 改装为全自动步枪的开源模型文件首次亮相；正是在这一年，出现了众筹的基因测序开源硬件。尽管 3D 打印会引发大量微不足道的抱怨，但美国南方的法官和伊朗的穆拉们，绝对会因为管辖区内有人打印性玩具而抓狂。而未来的走向……

cues.en: The trajectory of 3D printing will most certainly raise real grievances, from solid-state meth labs to ceramic knives. And it doesn't take a science fiction writer to understand why regulators might be nervous about the user-modifiable firmware on self-driving cars, or limiting interoperability for aviation controllers, or the kind of thing you could do with bioscale assemblers and sequencers. Imagine what will happen the day that Monsanto determines that it's really, really—
cues.zh: 3D 打印的发展轨迹必然会引发真正的社会矛盾，从固态冰毒作坊到陶瓷刀具，不一而足。不用科幻作家提醒，人们也能理解监管机构为何会焦虑：比如自动驾驶汽车上允许用户修改的固件，或是限制航空管制设备的互操作性，亦或是利用生物尺度的合成仪与测序仪可能造出的东西。想象一下，如果哪天 Monsanto 认定这件事真的、真的——

cues.en: important to make sure that computers can't execute programs that cause specialized peripherals to output organisms that eat their lunch, literally. Regardless of whether you think these are real problems or merely hysterical fears, they are nevertheless the province of lobbies and interest groups that are far more influential than Hollywood and big content are on their best day, and every one of them will arrive at the same place.
cues.zh: 极其重要：必须确保计算机无法运行特定程序，去操控专用外设制造出抢他们饭碗——字面意义上吃掉他们作物的生物。无论你认为这些是迫在眉睫的真问题，还是危言耸听的瞎操心，它们都已成为游说集团和利益团体的核心诉求，而这些势力的影响力，远非好莱坞和内容巨头最辉煌时所能比拟，而且他们最终都会得出同一个结论。

cues.en: Can't you just make us a general purpose computer that runs all the programs except for the ones that scare and anger us? Can't you just make us an internet that transmits any message over any protocol between any two points unless it upsets us? And personally, I can see that there will be programs that run on general purpose computers and peripherals that will even freak me out.
cues.zh: “难道你们就不能造出一台通用计算机，能运行所有的程序，除了那些让我们害怕和愤怒的吗？难道你们就不能打造一个互联网，能在任意两点之间通过任意协议传输任何信息，除非它让我们不爽吗？”而就我个人而言，我也能预见到，未来在通用计算机和外设上运行的某些程序，甚至连我自己都会感到毛骨悚然。

cues.en: So I can believe that people who advocate for limiting general purpose computers will find receptive audiences for their positions. But just as we saw with the copyright wars, banning certain instructions or protocols or messages will be wholly ineffective as a means of prevention and remedy. And as we saw in the copyright wars, all attempts at controlling PCs will converge on rootkits. All attempts at controlling the internet will converge on surveillance and censorship.
cues.zh: 所以我相信，主张限制通用计算机的人会为他们的立场找到愿意接受的听众。但正如我们在版权战争中所见，禁止某些指令、协议或消息，作为预防和补救手段将完全无效。而且正如版权战争所示，一切控制 PC 的尝试最终都会落到 rootkit 上。一切控制互联网的尝试最终都会走向监控和审查。

Or Facebook isn't as entertaining as you feel like it is. And in fact, both of those, they are. I think what we need to convey is all the ways in which it fails that are not immediately obvious at the outset. And that's a hard problem. I hear we have another question from the mighty internets.
cues.zh: 我发现的问题在于，我们往往倾向于攻击别人的长处。我们会说：哦，Apple 的整合并没有你想象的那么好。或者 Facebook 并没有你感觉的那么有趣。但事实上，这两者确实都很出色。我认为我们需要传达的，是它在初期并不显而易见的各种失效方式。而这是个难题。听说神通广大的网友又提了一个问题。

cues.en: Can you please say something about the difference between Europe and the USA and if they are some thing of a feedback loop and driving each other in the wrong direction? So the question is the feedback loop between America and Europe and or the USA in Europe and and what direction they go in I mean obviously
cues.zh: 能否请您谈谈欧洲和美国之间的差异，以及它们之间是否存在某种反馈循环，正把彼此推向错误的方向？那么问题就是美欧之间、或者说美国与欧洲之间的反馈循环，以及它们的发展方向。我的意思是，很显然……

cues.en: There is this transatlantic table tennis in terms of copyright that we've had before, where you get term extension, an extension of the length of copyright in America, and then Europe has to harmonize with America by extending its copyright to even longer than America. And then America has to harmonize with Europe to make its copyright longer than Europe's, and so on.
cues.zh: 在版权方面，我们以前就见过这种跨大西洋的“乒乓推拉球”：美国延长了版权保护期，欧洲为了与美国接轨，就必须把版权期延长得比美国还长；接着美国为了与欧洲接轨，又得把版权期改得比欧洲更长，如此循环往复。

cues.en: But increasingly, the way that that kind of stuff happens is in these really secretive and sinister treaty negotiations, like ACTA and the Trans-Pacific Partnership, where you have treaties negotiated by European and American representatives, but without any representatives from the governments. They're done by their administrations, without any transparency into it, and then it's presented as a fait accompli.
cues.zh: 但现在这类事情越来越常发生在极其隐秘、阴暗的条约谈判中，比如 ACTA 和 Trans-Pacific Partnership。在这些谈判中，条约是由欧美代表磋商的，却没有任何民选政府代表参与。它们完全由行政官僚敲定，毫无透明度可言，然后被直接当作既成事实强加下来。

cues.en: I think that there's not much difference because they're both getting shitty laws in the same way now. They're coming out of the same source. And they're not really American companies. I mean, EMI is technically kind of a British company, and Bertelsmann is technically a German company, and Holtzbrink is technically a German company, and Holtzbrink is too, and so on and so forth. Sony is technically Japanese, right? Okay, we've got another question from the audience. Yes, so you had...
cues.zh: 我觉得其实没太大区别，因为它们现在都以同样的方式受到那些操蛋法律的影响。这些法律都来自同一个源头。而且它们其实算不上是美国公司。我是说，EMI严格来说算是一家英国公司，Bertelsmann严格来说是德国公司，Holtzbrinck严格来说也是德国公司，等等等等。Sony严格来说是日本的，对吧？好的，台下还有个观众提问。是的，你有……

cues.en: Quite a few questions. I'm your rambling guy for today. Short. I really like the analogy of the five-year plan and the next five-year plan and the next five-year plan because I come from Poland and we know how the five-year plans in Poland went. So, I have this feeling that those five-year plans will probably end up just like they ended up in Poland. That's where...
cues.zh: 好几个问题。我今天就负责抛砖引玉了。尽量简短点。我真的很喜欢五年计划接下一个五年计划、再接下一个五年计划这个类比，因为我来自波兰，我们深知波兰当年的五年计划是什么结果。所以，我有种感觉，这些五年计划的下场大概会跟波兰当年的结局一模一样。那就是……

cues.en: what you think about that goes. Yeah, so and that's probably an extension of what this gentleman over here said when I finished a little out of turn, which was if this has the trajectory of the drug war, where the hell are we going to end up? Because obviously the drug war has been a disaster, continues to be a disaster, and shows no sign of receding from its disastrousness. And the difference is that although, you know, I guess there are people who would argue that drugs deliver a certain
cues.zh: 想听听你对此怎么看。是的，这大概也是顺着刚才那位先生的话往下聊，我之前有点抢话了，他当时问的是：如果这事沿着禁毒战争的轨迹发展，我们到底会沦落到什么地步？因为很显然，禁毒战争一直是一场灾难，现在依然是灾难，而且毫无灾难平息的迹象。而不同之处在于，尽管，你知道，我想有人会辩称毒品能在某种程度上

cues.en: certain bit of the solution to their own problem. In other words, once you've taken the right drugs, you no longer see the problem with drugs. And I don't mean that sarcastically. I mean, all due respect to my friends on the drug legalization side and the idea of cognitive liberty and the rest of it. But it's not the same way that computers hold the key to unlocking computers. Because what computers do, what networks do, is they make it cheaper and easier for us to do things together.
cues.zh: 在某种程度上解决自身带来的问题。换句话说，一旦你吸了对的药，你就不再觉得毒品是个问题了。我这不是在讽刺。我是说，我对支持毒品合法化、主张认知自由等观点的朋友们保持充分尊重。但这跟计算机掌握着解开计算机之谜的钥匙完全不是一回事。因为计算机和网络的作用，是让我们共同做事的成本更低、更容易。

cues.en: So, you know, in contrast to the, to, and with, again, with respect to my friend of Genny Morozov, in contrast to the things that he says, I, I'm much more optimistic about what computers can do for justice struggles, because by definition, people in charge have already figured out how to coordinate their actions, right? That's how they got to be in charge. So giving them technology to make them better coordinated is a small incremental improvement, whereas people who are oppressed,
cues.zh: 所以，你知道，相比于，而且再次声明，也是出于对我朋友 Evgeny Morozov 的尊重，与他的观点不同，我对于计算机在正义抗争中所能发挥的作用要乐观得多，因为从定义上讲，掌权者早就摸索出了协调行动的方法，对吧？他们就是这么掌权的。因此，给他们提供能更好协调的技术，只是一种微小的渐进式改进，而那些被压迫的人，

cues.en: by definition, have no capacity to steer the state and work collectively. Adding the capacity to work collectively to people who are at the bottom is a phase change for them in a way that it's not.
cues.zh: 从定义上讲，根本没有能力操纵国家机器、无法进行集体协作。为处于底层的人赋予集体协作的能力，对他们而言是一场质的飞跃，这种改变是截然不同的。

cues.en: It's a difference in kind and not just a difference in degree. And so I think that computers and networks allow us to do stuff together that we could never have done before. And the more computers and networks we get, the more things we can do together with them. There was this kind of tedious thing that happened about six or eight months ago whenever I mentioned the word anonymous in public. I would say anonymous is a group that. And someone come along and go, they're not a group.
cues.zh: 这是本质上的不同，而不仅仅是程度上的差异。所以我认为，计算机和网络让我们能够共同完成以前绝不可能做到的事情。我们拥有的计算机和网络越多，能借此协同完成的事情也就越多。大约六八个月前，每当我在公开场合提到 Anonymous 这个词时，总会发生一件挺烦人的事。我会说 Anonymous 是一个组织……然后就有人跳出来说，他们根本不是什么组织。

cues.en: And I'd say, anonymous last week did. And they'd say, anonymous never does anything. And I'd say, people using the name anonymous did. Well, they didn't all call themselves anonymous. Some of them called themselves low seconds. Some of them called themselves anti-says. And like, on and on and on. And for a while, I thought it was just a sort of tedious word game. You know, it's free, libre, open source. You know, this kind of endless kind of correct speak. But then I realized that it was actually because
cues.zh: 我会说，Anonymous 上周做了某事。他们会说，Anonymous 从来不做什么事。然后我会说，以 Anonymous 为名的人做了某事。可对方又说，他们又不全都自称 Anonymous，有些人自称 LulzSec，有些人自称 AntiSec。诸如此类，没完没了。有一阵子，我还以为这只是一种无聊的文字游戏。就像争论 Free、Libre 还是开源一样，你知道的，就是这种没完没了的所谓“正确表述”。但后来我意识到，这其实是因为……

cues.en: Anonymous and many other new kinds of institutions that we've seen in the last year are novel, that we don't actually have a vocabulary. There's something new on this earth, this kind of affinity organization that...
cues.zh: Anonymous 以及我们在过去一年中见到的许多新型组织形态都是前所未有的，我们实际上缺乏相应的词汇来描述。它们是这世界上诞生的新事物，这种志趣相投的群体组织……

cues.en: doesn't have the same hierarchical structures, even if there are pockets of leadership their way that there are with a non-ops or with bits of Occupy being spokespeople or coordinators. It's not anything like what these institutions would have been 10 or 20 years ago. You couldn't have had anything on the scale of Occupy, simultaneous coordinated actions in cities all over the world. You couldn't possibly have had that without a big sort of military style command and control organization.
cues.zh: 并没有以往那样的层级结构，即使偶尔会有一些小圈子的领导核心，比如 AnonOps，或者 Occupy 运动中充当发言人或协调员的群体。这与一二十年前的那些组织形态截然不同。在过去，你绝不可能发起像 Occupy 那样规模的行动，在世界各地的各大城市同时协同开展。要是没有一个庞大的、类似军事化的指挥控制组织，你根本不可能做到这一点。

cues.en: prior to the network, prior to the internet. And so we lack of vocabulary to describe them. We lack of vocabulary even to think about them in some ways. So we say, oh, Occupy doesn't have a set of unitary goals. They must not be serious. What's interesting is that prior to this, assembling a big organization without first agreeing on your goals was...
cues.zh: 在网络出现之前，在互联网普及之前，确实如此。所以我们缺乏词汇来描述它们，在某种程度上，我们甚至缺乏用来思考它们的词汇。因此我们才会说，噢，Occupy 连一套统一的目标都没有，他们肯定不是认真的。有趣的是，在此之前，如果不先就目标达成一致，就组织起一个庞大的机构，那简直是……

cues.en: cosmically insane because you put all this energy into organizing, and then it would turn out that you weren't all there for the same reason. You'd have to all go home again. And now what we can do is we can all get together and figure out the stuff that we agree on, our minimum common agreement, our TCPIP of protest.
cues.zh: 荒谬至极，因为你倾注了所有的精力去组织，结果却发现大家的出发点根本不一样，最后只能各回各家。而现在我们能做的是，大家聚在一起，找出我们达成的共识，也就是我们最低限度的共同协议，堪称抗议活动中的 TCP/IP 协议。

cues.en: And then we can work on that stuff. And then when we come to some stuff that we don't agree on, we can all go off and have a different occupy over there to do that stuff because the organizing itself has been cheap. It's no longer the case that the job of an activist is 98% stuffing envelopes and 2% figuring out what to put in them. Now we get the envelope stuffing for free, and we get to spend 100% of our time figuring out how to do stuff together. And so I do think that there is hope because the...
cues.zh: 然后我们就可以围绕这些共识开展行动。当遇到意见不合的事情时，大家完全可以分道扬镳，在别处发起另一场 Occupy 运动来做那些事，因为组织本身的成本已经变得极低。现在的情况不再是活动家 98% 的工作都在装信封，只有 2% 的时间在思考信里该写什么。如今装信封的工作几乎零成本，我们可以把 100% 的精力都用来思考如何协同合作。所以我深信这里面充满希望，因为……

cues.en: The terrain is not the same as the terrain in the war on drugs. OK, we've got like, where are we? We've got like 10 minutes here. So I'm going to ask Corey. Corey, you've got like 10 minutes. I think that's like five questions. So why don't we take like three questions, then I'll answer as many of them as I can. OK, cool. All right. So on the right hand side, this gentleman here. OK, so I think it might become harder to influence the minds in government in the right direction.
cues.zh: 这里的局势和禁毒战争的情况可不一样。好了，我们还有……到哪了？我们大概还有10分钟。那我问下Corey。Corey，你大概还有10分钟。我觉得差不多够提5个问题。要不我们先接3个问题，然后我尽量多回答一些。好的，太棒了。行，那右边这位先生请讲。好，我觉得想引导政府往正确的方向思考可能会越来越难。

cues.en: because we are sending mixed signals. On the one hand, we're talking about how they should chill and lay off the DRM and copyright war. While on the other hand, we are creating technology like Bitcoin or similar stuff that we don't beat at the money that the lobbyists get. We are creating things that are competing with the Reichsbank and the Fed. And now you're getting the government really pissed.
cues.zh: 因为我们释放的信号自相矛盾。一方面，我们劝他们冷静点，别再搞DRM和版权战争了。但另一方面，我们又搞出了像Bitcoin之类的技术，虽然比不过说客拿到的那些钱，但我们创造的东西是在直接和帝国银行、美联储竞争。这下你可把政府彻底惹毛了。

cues.en: I mean, I'm a big proponent of that. I mean, not the Fed, but Bitcoin or stuff like that. So, yeah, what do you think about that? Right. Two more questions. Okay. Next. Okay. I'm not allowed to hold the mic. Sorry. Question was, general proposed computers versus appliances. You said the threat is mostly by the lawmakers.
cues.zh: 我是说，我非常支持这种技术。不是支持美联储，而是支持Bitcoin这类东西。所以，对，你怎么看？好的，再来两个问题。好的，下一位。好的，主办方不让我拿话筒，不好意思。我的问题是，关于通用计算机与专用设备。你刚才说威胁主要来自立法者。

cues.en: One guy before went in this direction, I'm going. The problem I'm seeing is that we already do have these appliances. Even in this audience, people own iPhones and iPads. We have Kindles at homes, we have PlayStations and Xboxes. The list goes on and on and on. So even we, we want this stuff because it has good features. You try to answer in this direction. I was curious if you have anything more to say.
cues.zh: 前面有人也问了类似方向的问题。我看到的问题是，我们现在其实已经拥有了这些专用设备。就连在场的观众里，大家也有iPhone和iPad。我们家里有Kindle，有PlayStation和Xbox。这样的例子数不胜数。所以连我们自己都很想要这些东西，因为它们功能很棒。你刚才试着往这个方向回答了一下，我想知道你还有什么要补充的吗。

cues.en: I think this is more of the problem. Okay, one more. And then I'll try and answer them all in one go. Okay, do you think movement will develop to change the moral perception of computing like dare to make us feel bad about computing? And do you think hypocrisy develop among powerful people to say, well, when I was young, I programmed a computer, but it didn't inhale.
cues.zh: 我觉得这才是更大的问题。好的，再接一个问题。然后我试着一次性全回答了。好的，你觉得未来会不会出现一场运动，来改变人们对计算的道德认知，比如像DARE禁毒计划那样，让我们对使用计算机产生负罪感？而且你觉得权贵们会不会变得虚伪，说什么“我年轻时也编过程，但我可没真正陷进去”？

cues.en: All right, so the first two questions the question about Bitcoin and the question about why we why we continue to use these devices that even though they contain our own chains in some ways of the same question, right because we The reason that we
cues.zh: 好的，前两个问题——关于Bitcoin的问题，以及我们为什么明知这些设备在某种程度上束缚了自己，却依然继续使用它们的问题——其实问的是同一回事，对吧？因为我们……我们之所以

cues.en: use these devices is because they work, and we're pretty sanguine about their failure modes, because we're technocrats. We're like, oh, well, if they lock down my iPad, I know how to jailbreak it. If I ever want to run some code on it that someone else won't let me, I know how to do it. I've got a runtime on my computer. I can take my apps off of here and run them there, and so on. So we're very sanguine about it.
cues.zh: 使用这些设备，是因为它们确实好用，而且我们对它们的失效模式相当乐观，因为我们是技术官僚。我们会觉得，“哦，要是他们封锁了我的iPad，反正我知道怎么越狱。如果我想在上面跑一段别人不让我跑的代码，我知道该怎么做。我电脑上有运行时环境。我可以把应用从这里导出来放到那里跑”，诸如此类。所以我们对此非常乐观。

cues.en: We tend not to worry that that the consequences are going to come up and bite us in the ass But that's not all that different from lots of other ways in which people tend to overestimate their immortality I mean I felt that way you know I bought DRM media once I once bought thousands of dollars worth of audible books over the period of several years and it wasn't until I switched to an operating system that audible didn't have a player for that I realized that I was gonna have to spend a month and
cues.zh: 我们往往不担心会有恶果反噬到自己头上，但这跟人们在很多其他方面总觉得自己能长生不死并无两样。我是说，我自己也有过这种心态，我买过带 DRM 的媒体，我曾经在好几年的时间里买过价值数千美元的 Audible 有声书，直到我换了一个 Audible 没有播放器的操作系统，我才意识到我得花上整整一个月，

cues.en: running two power books all the time through an audio capture app to get all those audio books out of the proprietary wrapper and into something I could play back. And then I went, oh my god, I'm an idiot. But I was also a smoker, right? And I also sometimes forget to put on my seat belt. I mean, there's lots of ways in which we do this. And if we have to be pure in order to fight, then we'll probably never succeed. I mean, we have to admit that we live in the world and we sometimes
cues.zh: 一直开着两台 PowerBook，通过音频抓取软件把所有那些有声书从专有格式外壳中提取出来，转成我能播放的格式。当时我心想：天啊，我真是个白痴。但我以前还抽烟，对吧？我有时也会忘了系安全带。我是说，我们在很多方面都是这样。如果我们非得做到无可挑剔才能去抗争，那我们可能永远都不会成功。我们必须承认我们生活在现实世界中，有时我们

cues.en: either make mistakes or misjudge consequences or just do the thing that's most convenient and that's how life goes. The question about whether or not it's wise to piss them off while we're fighting them, you know, I don't think they could be any more...
cues.zh: 要么会犯错，要么会误判后果，要么就纯粹图方便，生活就是这样。至于在我们与他们抗争时去惹毛他们是否明智，我觉得，他们对互联网的恐惧

cues.en: afraid of the internet. I don't think that the thing that they most fear is Bitcoin. I think the thing that they most fear is all the disruption that arises from the internet, and Bitcoin's not the major disruptive application of the internet over the last several years. It's things like Amazon, and it's things like automated high-speed trading, and so on. All these things that are kind of legitimate Fortune 100 halls of power stuff.
cues.zh: 已经不可能更深了。我认为他们最害怕的并不是 Bitcoin。我认为他们最怕的是互联网带来的一切颠覆，而 Bitcoin 并不是这几年来互联网上最具颠覆性的主要应用。反而是像 Amazon、自动化高频交易等等诸如此类的东西。所有这些可以说是来自《财富》100 强权力殿堂里的合规事物，

cues.en: that has been most disruptive and that has got people running around like headless chickens. Bitcoin is just a thing over on the side. The number of people in the halls of power who understand it is minuscule, and the number who take it seriously is a fraction of them. And that's even true of cryptographers, not just people in the halls of power.
cues.zh: 才是最具颠覆性的，才让那些人急得像无头苍蝇一样乱撞。Bitcoin 不过是边缘角落里的一个小东西。权力殿堂里真正懂它的人寥寥无几，而严肃对待它的人更是少之又少。不仅是权力高层，甚至在密码学家当中也是如此。

cues.en: And then the last question was, will there be a dare to stop using computers movement in the future? I think we've already got it now, don't we? I once gave a, I write young adult novels sometimes as well as novels for adults. And I did the Young Adult Breakfast at the American Library, or at the Book Expo America, which is a big book expo show in America where all the booksellers come. And they have all the young adult booksellers show up, and they have a celebrity come and introduce the three young adult...
cues.zh: 然后最后一个问题是，未来会不会出现一场“敢于不用电脑”的运动？我想我们现在就已经有了，不是吗？我曾经参加过一次……我有时也写青少年小说和成人小说。我参加了美国图书馆、或者说全美书展（Book Expo America）上的青少年读物早餐会，那是美国一个大型书展，所有的书商都会来。所有青少年书商都会到场，他们还会请一位名人来介绍这三位青少年小说……
